reading.body:
AI intellectual property risk has split into ten distinct coverage lines, spanning training data scraping, model output infringement, and licence breaches.

The ten points cluster around three stages of the AI lifecycle. Data acquisition risks include scraping class actions, privacy violations, trade secret contamination, and cross-border jurisdiction. Output risks include patent invalidity, provenance failures, right of publicity, and synthetic data degradation. Licensing and indemnity risks include open weight non-compliance and hyperscaler indemnification in practice.

For AI builders, this means liability is not a single training data problem but a set of separate, insurable failure modes that can emerge after deployment. The inclusion of hyperscaler indemnification and open weight licence terms shows that even standard protections leave residual exposure. The data does not cover premiums, claim outcomes, or how often these policies are actually triggered, so it cannot measure cost or effectiveness.
